text: In September 2018, twenty of us reached for "the supreme court" on the twenty-eighth, and twenty of us said "of sexual assault" the day before. On that same day, the twenty-seventh, nineteen of us named "christine blasey ford," and nineteen of us said "senate judiciary committee." First-said among us on September 16, "christine blasey ford" was the only one of these phrases that began in this era; the rest we had carried since 2013. Twenty of us said "energy and water" on the thirteenth. Nineteen said "health and human services" on the twenty-sixth. On the seventeenth, nineteen of us said "the opioid crisis" and eighteen said "the opioid epidemic," two phrasings of one thing, one day apart. We converged on the hearing and on the court, and the record shows we said the same names on the same days.
